title: Tanker hit by projectile in Strait of Hormuz, 11 Indian crew injured
excerpt: A UK maritime agency reported the strike on 8 October, after which the UN halted its escort of ships through Hormuz.

notes: The headline, lede and key points must go to the 9 October strike on the GEM NO. 2, the only attack on a merchant ship inside the 24 hour window, hit 13 nm west of Al Jazeera Al Hamra in the Persian Gulf with the fire extinguished and all 22 crew safe. The 11 Indian crew injured are the 5 October On Peace attack off Oman, per India's Ministry of External Affairs, and the UN escort pause is the June 2026 Ever Lovely incident, so that sentence must go.

The 8 October Hormuz record is UKMTO's delayed report of a crude oil tanker struck at 1709 GMT on 6 October with no casualties: give it that date, and do not call it Panama-flagged or report 11 injured, because both of those details are the 5 October On Peace's.

The Black Sea item is the 6 October Aframax Rio strike, Liberia-flagged, 23 Indian crew rescued, nobody hurt: give it one Earlier in the week line with its 6 October date, not 8 to 9 October. The 10 crew killed in that entry belong to the 6 October sinking of the Alfa Watan, and India's injured-sailor condemnation to the 5 October Royad Mammadov strike.
